clue.text: Double prizewinner's a chap to reveal secrets to an audience

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: to an audience means the word is heard spoken rather than read, so we take its sound

parts.note: to reveal secrets is to tell, as in telling tales

explanation.surface: A two-time award winner is the sort of fellow who spills secrets in front of a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to an audience' signals that TELL is heard, giving the sound written TEL. Hilary Mantel won the Booker Prize twice, for Wolf Hall and Bring Up the Bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilary Mantel won the Booker twice, making her a two-time laureate of that award.

clue.text: German, say, endlessly entertaining about spies

indicators.note: about says the trimmed word wraps around the spies
endlessly says the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: entertaining means amusing
the CIA is the American spy agency

explanation.surface: A German is described as endlessly entertaining on the subject of espionage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German' looks like a nationality, but it is the English composer Edward German. 'endlessly' drops the outer letters and 'about' wraps the result round the spies.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edward German was an English composer of light opera, an example of a music-maker.

clue.text: Capek's warrior we hear, one represented in two sides, supporting neither

indicators.note: we hear means the word is taken by its sound and spelt differently

parts.note: Karel Capek wrote the novel War with the Newts, in which newts fight mankind

indicators.note: represented in says the single letter goes inside the pair of sides

parts.note: the two sides are right and left, R and L
one is A, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: A Czech writer's soldier is pictured within two factions while backing none of them.
explanation.walkthrough: Capek's War with the Newts has amphibian armies; 'we hear' turns NEWT into NEUT. 'represented in' places A inside R and L, the right and left sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone neutral takes no side in a dispute, favouring neither party.

clue.text: Established Church disrupted first of Scottish Celtic philosophers

parts.note: E is a standard abbreviation for established
C is a standard abbreviation for church

indicators.note: disrupted says the following letters are thrown into a new order
first of means just the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: An established Church is upset by early Scottish Celtic thinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupted' rearranges S (the 'first of Scottish') with CELTIC to make LECTICS, after E and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclectics were thinkers who chose doctrines from several schools rather than following one system.

clue.text: Travel by car carrying money for prizewinner

parts.note: to travel is to go

indicators.note: carrying says the car holds the money inside it

parts.note: RR, for Rolls-Royce, stands for a car
a dime is a coin, a small amount of money

explanation.surface: Driving somewhere with cash on board, in pursuit of a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: RR stands for Rolls-Royce, a crossword shorthand for a car. Nadine Gordimer shared the 1974 Booker Prize.
explanation.definitionFit: Nadine Gordimer won the Booker in 1974 and later the Nobel Prize for Literature.

clue.text: Dope is confused about University buildings — it's a department of psychology

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters go round the university letter
confused says these letters are muddled into another order

parts.note: taken as written
a complex is a group of buildings

explanation.surface: An idiot gets lost around the campus buildings, which house a psychology department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' turns DOPE IS into OEDIPS, and 'about' wraps that round U to give OEDIPUS; COMPLEX follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Freud's theory of a child's desire for the opposite-sex parent is a major area within psychoanalytic thought.

clue.text: Avoids characters like Jemima and Donald

definitions.meaning: to avoid a blow is to dodge or duck it
Jemima Puddle-Duck and Donald are famous cartoon and storybook waterfowl

explanation.surface: Someone dodges a pair of famous cartoon birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodging means bobbing down out of the way, and Jemima and Donald are both web-footed birds.

clue.text: Conrad narrator, English detective

definitions.meaning: Charlie Marlow tells the story of Heart of Darkness and other Joseph Conrad tales
Philip ... is the private eye created by Raymond Chandler, who was schooled in England

explanation.surface: A storyteller in a Conrad novel doubles as a sleuth.
explanation.walkthrough: Conrad's narrator is usually spelt Marlow, without the final E; the setter treats the two as one name.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to Conrad's storyteller and to Chandler's private investigator.

clue.text: Minstrel's merry dancing around start of hooley

indicators.note: around says the jumbled letters go round the single letter
dancing says the letters of the word move about into a new order
start of means the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A minstrel is cheerfully dancing at the beginning of an Irish party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' turns MERRY into RYMER, and 'around' puts H (the 'start of hooley') inside. A hooley is an Irish word for a lively party.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhymer is a maker of verses, like a medieval minstrel.

clue.text: Tense chap, one with reservations, investigates, we hear, annual award

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
a chap is a he
a booker is someone who makes bookings or reservations

indicators.note: we hear means the word is taken by its sound and given a different spelling

parts.note: to investigate nosily is to pry, so investigates is pries

explanation.surface: A nervous man with bookings snoops about, we are told, for a yearly honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One with reservations' suggests doubts, but it is someone who books. 'we hear' turns PRIES into PRIZE.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's leading literary honour for fiction is presented every year.

clue.text: With singular Greyfriars master education's suppressed

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
Mr Quelch is the form master at Greyfriars School in the Billy Bunter stories
ED is short for education

explanation.surface: A strict schoolmaster puts down any learning.
explanation.walkthrough: Greyfriars is the fictional school of Frank Richards's Billy Bunter stories, a British boys' classic.
explanation.definitionFit: Squelched means crushed or silenced, as a protest is put down.

clue.text: Have affection, yen, for prizewinner

parts.note: to have affection is to care
Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: Feeling fondness and a yearning for an award winner.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Carey won the Booker twice, for Oscar and Lucinda and True History of the Kelly Gang.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Carey is an Australian novelist who took the Booker in 1988 and 2001.

clue.text: With which to feed bucking bronco about start of circus?

definitions.text: With which to feed bucking bronco about start of circus?

indicators.note: about says the scrambled letters go round the single letter
bucking says the letters of the horse leap about into a new order
start of means only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: What to give a rodeo horse as feed at the beginning of a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bucking' shuffles BRONCO into CORNOB, and 'about' wraps it round C, the 'start of circus'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ear of maize is fodder one might offer a horse, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Ancient Shakespearean given base old coin

parts.note: Ancient Pistol is the swaggering ensign in Henry IV and Henry V
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: An aged character from Shakespeare is handed a debased antique piece of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ancient' is not 'old' but a military rank, ensign; Shakespeare's Pistol holds it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pistole was a gold coin used in Spain and elsewhere in Europe in past centuries.

clue.text: They were instrumental at law in France

parts.note: au is French for at the
loi is the French word for law

explanation.surface: Some people played a key part in a French courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in France' tells us both words are French.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Greek reed pipes were played in pairs, so they were musical tools in the literal sense.

clue.text: Sikes initially leading Bullseye, say, into old base that's concealed

indicators.note: into says the pieces go inside the other word

parts.note: a bed is a base, as a flower bed or bed of a road

indicators.note: leading says the letter comes in front of the next piece
initially means only the first letter of the word is used

parts.note: Bull's-eye is Bill Sikes's dog in Oliver Twist, a cur

explanation.surface: Dickens's villain leads his dog into an old hideout that is hidden away.
explanation.walkthrough: In Oliver Twist, Bill Sikes's dog is called Bull's-eye; 'say' signals an example of a cur. S and CUR go 'into' O + BED.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscured means hidden from view, as clouds cover the sun.

clue.text: A onesie, such as Lincoln might have worn during the civil war?

definitions.meaning: a one-piece garment covering body and legs

definitions.text: such as Lincoln might have worn during the civil war?
definitions.meaning: Lincoln led the Union side in the American Civil War, so his outfit would be a Union one

explanation.surface: Imagining Abraham Lincoln in a one-piece sleepsuit during the war.
explanation.walkthrough: A union suit is American one-piece long underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: This one-piece undergarment covers torso and legs, like a modern all-in-one.

clue.text: College with space in the outskirts of Sydney — that's meaning a lot

parts.note: a poly is a polytechnic college

indicators.note: in says the space goes inside the outer letters
the outskirts of means the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: an em is a printer's space

explanation.surface: A college with room on the edge of an Australian city has lots of significance.
explanation.walkthrough: An em is a printer's unit of space; 'that's' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Linguists use the term for a word carrying many senses, so it signifies plenty.

clue.text: Get on with old royal sorcerer

parts.note: to get on in life is to prosper

explanation.surface: Getting ahead alongside an elderly magician-king.
explanation.walkthrough: Prospero is the deposed Duke of Milan and magician in Shakespeare's The Tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's magician in The Tempest is the rightful Duke of Milan.

clue.text: Rued his novel, did this previous prizewinner?

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A past award winner regretted his book, didn't he?
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book but signals the anagram. Salman Rushdie won the Booker for Midnight's Children.
explanation.definitionFit: Salman Rushdie took the 1981 Booker for Midnight's Children.

clue.text: Start with home stereo occasionally

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: occasionally says only every other letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Begin by playing a home hi-fi now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' picks the alternate letters T, R, O from stereo.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening section of a piece of music or a talk.

clue.text: Dismal winter overcomes Kanga finally — more like Owl

indicators.note: overcomes says the jumbled letters sit over and around the other letter
dismal suggests a poor state, so the letters are rearranged
finally means only the last letter of the name

explanation.surface: A gloomy winter defeats a kangaroo from Winnie-the-Pooh, making things more owlish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dismal' makes TWNIER from WINTER, and 'overcomes' wraps it round A, the last letter of Kanga.
explanation.definitionFit: Owl from Winnie-the-Pooh suggests the tawny owl, so tawnier means more brownish-orange like that bird.

clue.text: Korean henchman given occasional work

definitions.meaning: Goldfinger's Korean bodyguard in the James Bond story
a small one-off task, a casual piece of work

explanation.surface: A Korean heavy picks up some casual employment.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldfinger's hat-throwing bodyguard shares his name with casual handyman tasks.

clue.text: Where K stopped working, quietly leaving?

definitions.text: Where K stopped working, quietly leaving?

indicators.note: working says the letters are set to work in a new order

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

explanation.surface: A computer screen where the K key has died, so typing is silent.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of K STOPPED, less a P (quietly, from musical piano), rearrange to give the answer: a composite anagram signalled by 'working' and 'leaving'.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer's main screen is where a broken key would make itself felt, so the clue describes it.

clue.text: Sample section of Kant as text

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A philosophy student reads an extract from Kant as a set text.
explanation.definitionFit: To taste food is to try a little of it.

clue.text: Publishing house leads with novel attributed to prizewinner

indicators.note: leads means the opening letters of the two words before

parts.note: novel means new
a work by someone is attributed to them

explanation.surface: A publisher heads up a new book credited to an award-winning author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads' picks P and H, the first letters of Publishing house. P H Newby won the first Booker Prize in 1969.
explanation.definitionFit: P H Newby won the first Booker in 1969, for Something to Answer For.

clue.text: Character in Oklahoma in the part of a traitor

parts.note: Jud Fry is the farmhand villain in the musical Oklahoma!
as means playing the role of, as in Olivier as Hamlet

explanation.surface: An actor in Oklahoma! is cast as a betrayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character in Oklahoma' suggests a hidden letter, but it is Jud from the musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Judas Iscariot betrayed Jesus, so the name means any betrayer.

clue.text: Lacking scholarship, i.e. untried possibly?

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be put in some other order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters I and E

explanation.surface: Being unlearned means, that is, not yet tested, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges IE and UNTRIED together.
explanation.definitionFit: Inerudite means unlearned, without book learning.

clue.text: Opening with Elizabethan dramatist in audio guide

indicators.note: in audio means the words are heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: an opening is a bay, and Thomas Dekker was an Elizabethan playwright

explanation.surface: An audio guide starts with a playwright of the Elizabethan age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audio guide' reads as one thing, but 'in audio' is the sound signal and 'guide' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Karl Baedeker published famous travel handbooks, and his name stands for any travel handbook.

clue.text: Tale about European prizewinner

indicators.note: about says the tale is wrapped round the other letter

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A story about a European award winner.
explanation.walkthrough: David Storey won the Booker in 1976 for Saville.
explanation.definitionFit: David Storey took the 1976 Booker for his novel Saville.
